examples.explain: Lines at 1 and 5: width 4 × height min(7, 6) = 24.
The two outer lines: width 4 × height 4.

hints: Area = width × min(left height, right height). Trying all pairs is O(n²).
Start with the widest container. To possibly do better with a narrower one, which wall must change?
Always move the pointer at the shorter line - keeping it can never beat the current area.

insight.mnemonic: The short wall has nothing left to offer - drop it.
insight.oneLiner: Start wide; the shorter wall limits every narrower container that keeps it, so move the shorter wall inward.
insight.pattern: Two pointers, discard the limiting side

recall.a: The shorter one: any narrower container keeping it is capped by it and narrower, so it can't win.
Here only the two chosen walls matter (bars in between are ignored); in Trapping Rain Water every bar holds water.
recall.q: How is this different from Trapping Rain Water?

signals: value depends on min of the two ends × distance
insight.why: Each move eliminates every remaining pair involving the discarded wall, all of which are provably no better. So n − 1 moves cover all O(n²) pairs.

oneLiner: Start wide; the shorter wall limits every narrower container that keeps it, so move the shorter wall inward.

pitfalls.explain: Moving the taller wall can only shrink the area. Move the shorter one.
pitfalls.title: Moved the taller wall

pitfalls.explain: Water spills over the shorter line: area = width × min(h[l], h[r]).
pitfalls.title: Used the taller wall as the water level

solutions.idea: Compute the area for all pairs of walls and keep the maximum.
solutions.name: Try every pair

footnotes.text: Moving the taller wall can never help: the width shrinks and the height is still capped by the same shorter wall. Moving the shorter wall is the only move that might find a taller partner.

solutions.idea: Start with the widest container and repeatedly discard the shorter wall.
solutions.name: Two pointers from the outside in

starter:
class Solution:
    def maxArea(self, height: List[int]) -> int:
statement:
`height[i]` is the height of a vertical line at position `i`. Choose **two lines** that, together with the x-axis, form a container.

Return the **largest amount of water** a container can hold. The water level is limited by the shorter of the two lines, and the container's width is the distance between them. (The container can't be tilted.)
title: Container With Most Water
